component.name: Hop-tunes
component.summary: Local-first music player with private profiles

description.p: Hop-tunes is a calm, fast music player for the music files you already own. It works fully offline: no accounts, no sign-in, no store and no tracking.

ul.li: Gapless playback, optional crossfade and even volume (ReplayGain)
Browse by artist, album and song, with instant search and your own cover art
Playlists, smart playlists and import of m3u, pls, xspf and Zune zpl playlists
Quickplay: pinned favourites, recently played, new albums and an offline smart DJ
Local profiles so several people can share one computer, with an optional PIN
Dark and light themes, media keys and desktop media widgets

description.p: Hop-tunes is inspired by how the Zune desktop software organised music. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

description.p: Hop-tunes for Windows (experimental, install at your own risk: the developer never tests on Windows, only automated tests do; Windows testers wanted).

ul.li: A Windows 10/11 installer and a single-file portable exe, both with everything included.
Fixes replacing a damaged profile database on Windows.

description.p: Four new collection sections, video folders of their own, and your own video thumbnails.

ul.li: Pictures, audiobooks, ebooks and podcasts, each with its own folders and its own choose-folder button. Audiobooks, podcasts and ebooks remember where you stopped.
EPUB books open in a built-in reader; PDFs open in your PDF viewer.
The videos tab can have its own folders; existing libraries are unchanged.
An "image" button under each video lets you choose its thumbnail.

description.p: Fixes video playback, which never actually played after v1.2.0's locale fix.

ul.li: Video opened to a black, frozen screen with no picture or audio and no visible error — a QML call into the video surface silently failed before the video ever loaded. Confirmed fixed on real hardware (Steam Deck, CachyOS Handheld Edition).
Video rendered upside down; also confirmed fixed on the same hardware.

description.p: Quality-of-life release: per-profile album edits and drag-reorder everywhere, a tidier Quickplay.

ul.li: An album's cover and title can be edited right in the Collection grid, and its tracks dragged into a custom order live, even mid-playback. The songs tab now drags and reorders the same way too. All of it is per-profile and private — never seen by another profile sharing the same install.
Quickplay's pinned strip now groups into artists/albums/playlists sections instead of one mixed row.

description.p: Fixes video playback on real hardware.

ul.li: Video playback could fail to start with "mpv_create failed" depending on the system's locale, while music played fine — found testing v1.1.0 on a Steam Deck running CachyOS Handheld Edition. The video engine now works regardless of the desktop's locale settings.
Settings' folder list is now called "media folders" instead of "music folders", since it has fed both the music and video scanners since M7.

description.p: M7: video playback, and a step further toward always-offline.

ul.li: A collection › videos grid with thumbnails, codec/resolution/HDR badges, and a full-window player (libmpv, falling back to GStreamer where it isn't available) with subtitles and resume position
Live library updates: a song or video dropped into a watched folder appears without a manual rescan
The planned MusicBrainz lookup and podcasts (RSS) features were dropped before being built — neither fits an always-offline player
Local profiles with an optional PIN and guest mode
Playlists, smart playlists, playlist import and export, instant search
Quickplay with pins, history, new albums and an offline smart DJ
Crossfade, ReplayGain, shuffle and repeat, dark and light themes
Open music files from your file manager; a second launch reuses the open window

description.p: First preview: library scan, gapless playback, collection and now playing.
